text:
rachael: Quick sync — thinking out loud about the long-term roadmap for routing lanes, regional stitching, and tenant isolation. Need to align on launch criteria and what customer asks force into scope.

sam: +1. Can we start by listing the hard customer constraints? I have a couple from AcmeHealth (EU-only + low-latency), FinTechCo (SLA 99.95, dedicated capacity), and an internal analytics workload that needs cross-region burst.

minh: For AcmeHealth the ask is clear: traffic must not cross non-EU egress. They also want audit logs and KMS for keys. That basically forces Private or Dedicated in eu-west1.

jess: Important tradeoff: strict regional residency increases cost and complicates autoscaling. We should capture acceptance criteria: e.g., "no egress outside region under normal operation" + documented fallback when capacity exhausted.

rachael: Agreed. Draft launch criteria idea: 1) policy primitives (region affinity, hard-residency flag, tenant quiesce), 2) operational playbook (evacuation, quota bump workflow), 3) telemetry (per-tenant egress/latency/eviction events). If those are green, we mark feature GA for dedicated/private.

elena: Also add rollout gating: start with canary customers (1-2) + soak window 2 weeks + regression thresholds for latency (+p50/p95) and error rate.

sam: Customer asks that will be deferred: per-tenant cryptographic isolation (HSM-per-tenant) and sub-second cold-starts for large seq lengths. Flagging them as longer-term.

minh: On routing policy surface: propose two orthogonal knobs — affinity (soft) and residency (hard). Affinity aims to prefer region but can cross on overload. Residency is a strict policy. Need to decide which tiers get which by default.

rachael: Proposal: Hosted tier = affinity only. Dedicated = affinity + optional residency. Private = residency available and default. Thoughts?

jess: That maps to business tiers. But Sales will push Dedicated customers to expect residency. We'll need clear contract language. Also add cost delta guidance: e.g., +20-50% depending on bin packing efficiency.

elena: Operational constraints: when a region is degraded, do we fail closed (respect residency) or fail open (allow cross-region)? For regulated customers we should fail closed but provide emergency evict/approve flow. Need manual override + auditable justification.

ops-bot: auto-note: deployment window for routing policy engine planned in infra sprint 48. Impact: routing infra + policy DSL will be touched.

minh: Implementation sketch: policy DSL with rules like: `tenant.policy.residency = "eu-west1"` and `tenant.policy.affinity = [eu-west1, eu-central1]`. Runtime picks local pool if available else consult fallback list. Cache decisions per request for 30s.

sam: Perf note: cache TTL influences tail latency with cold rollouts. We must measure KV-cache hit rate when affinity holds vs when fallback triggers. Add to acceptance tests.

rachael: Action items: 1) Product to draft launch criteria and customer-facing contract language (jess + rachael) — due EOD Thurs. 2) Eng-arch to produce policy DSL proto + backfill test plan (minh + sam) — draft by Mon. 3) Ops to write evacuation + emergency override runbook (elena) — initial doc by next Wed. 4) PM to validate with AcmeHealth and FinTechCo (rachael).

jess: Minor: add telemetry surface to Redwood Console: per-route regional-breakdown and per-tenant residency-violations alerting. Ops also wants an elevated audit log sink for enterprise.

minh: I'll add a short config sample to the draft PR:
```
# example tenant policy
policy:
  residency: eu-west1      # hard residency
  affinity: [eu-west1, eu-central1]  # preference order
  fallback: allow-cross-region: false
```

rachael: Love it. Last thought: we should capture migration story for customers already on shared pools — a staged onboarding with capacity reservation windows, dry-run mode (policy enforced in log-only), and clear rollback. Include cost estimate model per tenant.

sam: I'll model cost deltas for small/med/large customers and share next Tue.

elena: I'll prototype the dry-run telemetry so we can validate without risking routing.

rachael: Great. If no objections, we'll take this to the next architecture sync and start customer outreach. :thumbsup:

jess: +1 

sam: +1

minh: +1
